thread:
pagerduty-bot: URGENT: Pager triggered for GPU inference pool (region-us-west). High queue growth and >95% GPU utilization. Autoscaler reported max node ceiling reached.

Alex (oncall): I see traffic spike and queue backlog on the inference queue. Autoscaler logs show max_nodes=32. Customers seeing 429s and increased latency.

Maya - SRE: Confirmed. metric:gpu_pool_utilization=98% over 5m, request_queue_length=~1200. Auto-scaler tried to scale but rejected due to node cap.

Sanjay (infra): Paging infra team. I can raise the pool to 48 but need approval and I'll toggle a manual override. Any objections?

Emily (support): Getting multiple customer escalations (enterprise accounts). Passing CS notes: "models timing out / throttled". We need ETA to share.

Alex (oncall): Approve manual bump. Prioritize enterprise traffic. Put canary rules to route high-tier customers to reserved nodes if possible.

Maya - SRE: Working on short-term mitigation: 1) manual node bump, 2) create a hot-path rule to route p99 requests to dedicated pool, 3) throttle low-priority batch work.

infra-bot: Deploy request accepted. Authorization: Alex (oncall). Initiating node pool update.

Sanjay (infra): Running infra command now:
```
# increase GPU node pool from 32 -> 48 (manual override)
infra-admin node-pool update --name=gpu-west --min=32 --max=48 --manual-override=true
```

Maya - SRE: While nodes spin up, we should apply immediate queue shedding for low-priority jobs. Patch to routing config: set priority=high for accounts A,B,C.

Alex (oncall): Patch applied. Command used:
```
rbx-route set-policy --queue inference --priority-map high:acctA,acctB,acctC --default low
```

Emily (support): Notifying affected customers with a short note: "We're seeing throttling due to a capacity event; we've raised capacity and routing priority for enterprise traffic. ETA ~10-15m."

infra-bot: Node pool update started. Expected node attach time ~6-8m.

Maya - SRE: Monitoring rolling attach. Also seeing some pending pods stuck on imagePullBackOff due to concurrent node provisioning surge — will watch.

Sanjay (infra): Node attach progressing: +8 nodes added in the first wave. Current nodes=40.

Alex (oncall): Good. Keep an eye on queue length and p95 latency. If Q drops and errors decrease, we'll keep nodes at 48 for now and schedule a follow-up to decide permanent cap.

Maya - SRE: Observability: queue_length-> 1200 -> 450 over 10m. p95 latency trending down from 2.5s to 900ms. 429s reduced.

Emily (support): Customers acknowledge update, one asking for SLA credit info. I've forwarded to CS manager.

Sanjay (infra): Full node count reached 48. Autoscaler still has max_nodes set to 48 in config. We should consider bumping the policy for future spikes or enable burst capacity.

Alex (oncall): We need a safe rollout plan for adjusting autoscale policies. Immediate action: keep manual override active for 30m, then hand off to next oncall for follow-up.

Maya - SRE: Agreed. Add a temporary autoscaler policy: allow burst to 64 for 15 minutes with cooldown. Command:
```
infra-admin autoscaler set --pool=gpu-west --burst-max=64 --burst-duration=15m --cooldown=10m
```

Sanjay (infra): Applied burst policy. Note: this requires ops approval for quota increase; I've filed request with cloud-quotas but burst is within emergency override window.

infra-bot: Alert: imagePullBackOffs cleared on new nodes. Pod scheduling resumed.

Alex (oncall): Handing off in 20 minutes to Maya. Key actions for next oncall: 1) observe cost impact, 2) validate autoscaler policy changes, 3) begin post-incident ticket with timeline and customer impact.

Maya - SRE: I'll take the handoff at +20. I'll draft an initial incident summary and customer-impact matrix.

Emily (support): Collecting a list of impacted accounts. Will attach timestamps and example request IDs to the incident ticket.

Alex (oncall): Quick note for postmortem: root cause likely traffic spike + autoscaler ceiling too conservative + lack of burst policy. Also check for any runaway background workers that could be contributing.

Sanjay (infra): I'll follow up on quota request and recommended permanent max_nodes. Also will review node provisioning speed — consider prewarmed standby nodes.

Maya - SRE: Logging the immediate mitigation steps in #incidents-log and creating a follow-up ticket: "Investigate autoscale ceiling and implement controlled burst/standby nodes".

Alex (oncall): Thanks everyone. Handing on-call to @Maya - SRE now. I'll remain available for escalation.

Maya - SRE: Taking handoff. Current status: nodes=48, queue_length=~420, p95=850ms, error-rate down to baseline. Postmortem owner: Maya.

Emily (support): I'll update customers once the postmortem timeline is available.

infra-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Recorded runbook steps executed: manual node bump, priority routing, burst policy applied.

Maya - SRE: Closing the active page. We'll keep this thread for follow-ups and the postmortem draft. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
